title: Adaptive tilting-wing configurations
description: A flying prototype investigates wing incidence across the multicopter flight envelope.
introduction: Wings can influence a quadrotor even when it is not operating as a fixed-wing aircraft. This ongoing project investigates whether adjusting their incidence can make that contribution useful across a wider range of speeds and attitudes.

problem.heading: The airflow changes with the flight condition.
paragraphs: A wing’s useful orientation depends on the local airflow. Forward motion, manoeuvring and propeller-induced flow create different conditions around a multicopter.
An orientation that helps in one part of the flight envelope may not help in another. The research question is how adjustable wing incidence can respond to those changing conditions.

approach.heading: Let the wing adapt to the local flow.
paragraphs: Building on observations from the trimodal platform, Diogo Nunes’s prototype replaces fixed wings with tilting wings. Their incidence can be adjusted as the vehicle changes speed or attitude.

The work considers forward-flight lift as well as the influence of propeller-induced airflow. The current research is directed at identifying useful orientations and measuring the resulting net energy benefit.

steps.title: Change the flight condition
steps.text: Consider hover, manoeuvring and forward flight.

steps.title: Adjust wing incidence
steps.text: Adapt the wing orientation to the local airflow.

steps.title: Evaluate the complete vehicle
steps.text: Measure the net effect rather than assuming that added lift guarantees lower energy use.

evidence.label: Flying prototype
evidence.text: The supplied recording demonstrates that the tilting-wing prototype is flying. It is evidence of prototype operation.

evidence.label: Research objective
evidence.text: An optimized incidence schedule and a quantified net energy benefit are ongoing research objectives, rather than established results of this demonstration.
